sections.theory:
Foods that are rich in protein are also excellent sources of phosphorus. These include meat and poultry, fish, eggs, milk and other dairy products.

Some non-protein food sources also contain phosphorus. For example, whole grains, potatoes, garlic, dry fruits and carbonated drinks.

Deficiency of Phosphorous

Deficiency of phosphorous in the body leads to various problems such as, joint or bone pain, loss of appetite, irritability or anxiety, fatigue and poor bone development in children.

Deficiency of phosphorous in children leads to renal rickets.

Excess of Phosphorous

Too much phosphate can be toxic.

An excess can cause diarrhoea, as well as a hardening of organs and soft tissues.

An increase in the plasma phosphate level due to decrease in its excretion leads to kidney dysfunction.

iv. Zinc

Zinc is antioxidant and important for the maintenance of a healthy immune system. Zinc is an important element for the normal growth, reproduction and longevity of animals.

Daily requirement

The recommended daily amount of zinc for an adult is 10 mg.

It is a constituent of several types of enzymes such as alkaline phosphatase, carbonic anhydrase etc.

It also forms a complex with insulin and helps in its storage and release according to the needs of the body. It is also required for maintaining the plasma concentration of vitamin A.

Sources of Zinc

The different sources of zinc include meat, liver, eggs, fish, milk and cereals.

Deficiency of Zinc

Deficiency of zinc results in slow healing of wounds, impairment of acuity of taste and skin problems.

Excess of Zinc

Excess intake of zinc can cause gastrointestinal discomfort and when chronic, may disrupt the balance of other chemicals in the body, including copper and iron.

sections.content:
Foods that are rich in protein are also excellent sources of phosphorus. These include meat and poultry, fish, eggs, milk and other dairy products.

Some non-protein food sources also contain phosphorus. For example, whole grains, potatoes, garlic, dry fruits and carbonated drinks.

Deficiency of Phosphorous

Deficiency of phosphorous in the body leads to various problems such as, joint or bone pain, loss of appetite, irritability or anxiety, fatigue and poor bone development in children.

Deficiency of phosphorous in children leads to renal rickets.

Excess of Phosphorous

Too much phosphate can be toxic.

An excess can cause diarrhoea, as well as a hardening of organs and soft tissues.

An increase in the plasma phosphate level due to decrease in its excretion leads to kidney dysfunction.

iv. Zinc

Zinc is antioxidant and important for the maintenance of a healthy immune system. Zinc is an important element for the normal growth, reproduction and longevity of animals.

Daily requirement

The recommended daily amount of zinc for an adult is 10 mg.

It is a constituent of several types of enzymes such as alkaline phosphatase, carbonic anhydrase etc.

It also forms a complex with insulin and helps in its storage and release according to the needs of the body. It is also required for maintaining the plasma concentration of vitamin A.

Sources of Zinc

The different sources of zinc include meat, liver, eggs, fish, milk and cereals.

Deficiency of Zinc

Deficiency of zinc results in slow healing of wounds, impairment of acuity of taste and skin problems.

Excess of Zinc

Excess intake of zinc can cause gastrointestinal discomfort and when chronic, may disrupt the balance of other chemicals in the body, including copper and iron.

sections.theory:
Key Points

Biochemistry studies the chemistry of life.

Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acid are called biomolecules.

Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes (aldoses) and polyhydroxy ketones (ketoses) or compounds formed by linking aldoses and ketoses.

Glucose is known as “aldose” and has an aldehyde structure at carbon atom number one.

Fructose is known as “ketose” and has a keto structure at carbon atom number two.

The main classes of carbohydrates are monosaccharide, oligosaccharide and polysaccharide.

Monosaccharides and oligosaccharides are collectively called sugars. Polysaccharides are non-sugars.

When two monosaccharide units combine together by an oxygen atom with elimination of one water molecule, this type of linkage is called glycosidic linkage or glycosidic bond.

Amino acids are monomers of proteins and they are connected by peptide bond in proteins.

The structure of protein is considered at four levels, primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary.

Lipids are heterogeneous class of organic compounds. They may be saponifiable or non-saponifiable.

The oils, which contain more unsaturation, are hydrogenated to produce solid ghee.

DNA and RNA are two examples of nucleic acid and their function is replication and protein synthesis.

The building blocks of nucleic acids are nucleotides.

The three components of a deoxyribonucleotide are a five-carbon sugar called deoxyribose, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base.

Enzymes are protein in nature, which can speed up a chemical reaction.

Enzyme inhibition may be irreversible or reversible.

Most animal enzyme’s optimum temperature is body temperature (37°C).

A pH, at which an enzyme shows the maximum activity, is called optimum pH.

امینو اسیدونه د پروټینونو مونومرونه دي او په پروټینونو کې د پېپټایډ تړون په واسطه نښتي دي.

حیاتی کیمیا زندگی کی کیمیا کا مطالعہ کرتی ہے۔

کاربوہائیڈریٹس، پروٹینز، لپڈز اور نیوکلک ایسڈ حیاتی سالمات کہلاتے ہیں۔

کاربوہائیڈریٹس پولی ہائیڈروآکسی الڈیہائیڈز (الڈوزز) اور پولی ہائیڈروآکسی کیٹونز (کیٹوزز) یا الڈوزز اور کیٹوزز کے جڑنے سے بننے والے مرکبات ہیں۔

گلوکوز کو ”الڈوز“ کہتے ہیں اور اس کے کاربن ایٹم نمبر ایک پر الڈیہائیڈ ساخت ہے۔

فرکٹوز کو ”کیٹوز“ کہتے ہیں اور اس کے کاربن ایٹم نمبر دو پر کیٹو ساخت ہے۔

کاربوہائیڈریٹس کی بڑی جماعتیں مونوسیکرائیڈ، اولیگوسیکرائیڈ اور پولی سیکرائیڈ ہیں۔

مونوسیکرائیڈز اور اولیگوسیکرائیڈز کو مجموعی طور پر شکر کہتے ہیں۔ پولی سیکرائیڈز غیر شکر ہیں۔

جب دو مونوسیکرائیڈ اکائیاں پانی کے ایک سالمے کے اخراج کے ساتھ ایک آکسیجن ایٹم کے ذریعے آپس میں جڑتی ہیں تو اس قسم کے ربط کو گلائیکوسائیڈک ربط یا گلائیکوسائیڈک بند کہتے ہیں۔

امائنو ایسڈز پروٹینز کے مونومر ہیں اور پروٹینز میں پیپٹائیڈ بند سے جڑے ہوتے ہیں۔

پروٹین کی ساخت کو چار سطحوں پر دیکھا جاتا ہے: ابتدائی، ثانوی، ثالثی اور چہارمی۔

لپڈز نامیاتی مرکبات کی متنوع جماعت ہیں۔ یہ قابلِ صابن سازی یا ناقابلِ صابن سازی ہو سکتے ہیں۔

زیادہ غیر سیر شدگی والے تیلوں کو ہائیڈروجنیٹ کر کے ٹھوس گھی بنایا جاتا ہے۔

DNA اور RNA نیوکلک ایسڈ کی دو مثالیں ہیں اور ان کا فعل نقل اور پروٹین کی تالیف ہے۔

نیوکلک ایسڈز کی بنیادی اکائیاں نیوکلیوٹائیڈز ہیں۔

ڈی آکسی رائبونیوکلیوٹائیڈ کے تین اجزا ڈی آکسی رائبوز نامی پانچ کاربن والی شکر، ایک فاسفیٹ گروپ اور ایک نائٹروجنی اساس ہیں۔

خامرے فطرتاً پروٹین ہیں جو کیمیائی تعامل کو تیز کر سکتے ہیں۔

خامروں کی روک تھام ناقابلِ واپسی یا قابلِ واپسی ہو سکتی ہے۔

زیادہ تر حیوانی خامروں کا موزوں ترین درجہ حرارت جسم کا درجہ حرارت (37°C) ہے۔

وہ pH جس پر خامرہ زیادہ سے زیادہ سرگرمی دکھاتا ہے، موزوں ترین pH کہلاتا ہے۔

sections.content:
Key Points

Biochemistry studies the chemistry of life.

Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acid are called biomolecules.

Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes (aldoses) and polyhydroxy ketones (ketoses) or compounds formed by linking aldoses and ketoses.

Glucose is known as “aldose” and has an aldehyde structure at carbon atom number one.

Fructose is known as “ketose” and has a keto structure at carbon atom number two.

The main classes of carbohydrates are monosaccharide, oligosaccharide and polysaccharide.

Monosaccharides and oligosaccharides are collectively called sugars. Polysaccharides are non-sugars.

When two monosaccharide units combine together by an oxygen atom with elimination of one water molecule, this type of linkage is called glycosidic linkage or glycosidic bond.

Amino acids are monomers of proteins and they are connected by peptide bond in proteins.

The structure of protein is considered at four levels, primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary.

Lipids are heterogeneous class of organic compounds. They may be saponifiable or non-saponifiable.

The oils, which contain more unsaturation, are hydrogenated to produce solid ghee.

DNA and RNA are two examples of nucleic acid and their function is replication and protein synthesis.

The building blocks of nucleic acids are nucleotides.

The three components of a deoxyribonucleotide are a five-carbon sugar called deoxyribose, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base.

Enzymes are protein in nature, which can speed up a chemical reaction.

Enzyme inhibition may be irreversible or reversible.

Most animal enzyme’s optimum temperature is body temperature (37°C).

A pH, at which an enzyme shows the maximum activity, is called optimum pH.
